newsitem.title: USA: Actor Charlie Sheen faces battery trial in Calif.
newsitem.headline: Actor Charlie Sheen faces battery trial in Calif.

text.p: Actor Charlie Sheen on Thursday was ordered to stand trial on May 30 for battery after his lawyers and attorneys for the woman he allegedly struck failed to reach a plea agreement.
Malibu Municipal Court Judge Lawrence Mira set the trial date after meeting for two hours behind closed doors with lawyers for both parties.
Sheen's lawyer Steve Cochran told reporters they had hoped to resolve the case with a plea agreement, but that discussions would continue. "We may be going to trial," he said.

Sheen, 31, the star of "Platoon," "Wall Street" and "Hot Shots," has been free on $20,000 bail since his arrest last December when Brittany Ashland claimed he knocked her unconscious during an argument at his suburban home.
The son of actor Martin Sheen and brother of movie star Emilio Estevez, he pleaded innocent to a misdemeanor count of battery with serious injury.
Ashland, who said she had dated Sheen for five months at the time of the argument, also filed a civil lawsuit alleging assault, battery, negligence, false imprisonment and emotional distress.
